prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Offshore wind farm O&M. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (Morrowick; sends Transformer Tap Snapshot on transformer review request), Main Transformer, export cable to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; dispatch boundary; authorized signals with transmission system). Public grid, external port ops out of scope. Personnel keep safety authority. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; blocks protection-conflicting commands; produces Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode if aux lost), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor (condition data), Turbine Sensor Bus (operating measurements); Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; blade imagery, inspection planning). Substation: Export Cable Monitor (cable condition), station service transformers, Emergency Generator (Foxglove). Aux power: auto start on loss; transfer within V/f limits; no unapproved paralleling; not exported; shed nonessential; start-failure alarm; UPS control power; transfer back when stable. Grid: Grid Dispatcher sets dispatch; Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard) allocates output, uses Position Quality Flag, assigns vessel/crew to approved work packages after Duty Planner confirms priority; Control Engineer verifies settings; frequency response only in authorized mode; comms loss keeps local protection; export resumes only when stable with protections; Substation Operator confirms switching and local constraints; alarms safety>protection>export. Shore: SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; work packages from Pitch Deviation Notice; Session Revocation Receipt), Shore Control Room (Amber Quay), Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; ranks work; uses Squall Window Bulletin), Operations Radio Console, Work Permit Portal (readiness for controlled access/isolation). Planning: Duty Planner reviews ranked queue, chooses mobilization, checks parts, competence, duration; safety/generation-loss faults over routine inspections; Field Supervisor validates faults, identifies offshore visits. Marine: Marine Coordinator (daily plan; matches conditions to vessels; coordinates changes with Vessel Master), Vessel Master, Weather Service (forecasts), Weather Analyst (forecast confidence); Weather Hold blocks mobilization beyond limits; Port Agent; Rescue Coordinator; HSE Officer (hazard review; Harness Audit Card); Storekeeper (validates Backorder Exception Slip). Vessels: Crew Transfer Vessel (Kestrel Bay), Daughter Craft, Service Operations Vessel; Helideck; Vessel AIS Receiver (Blue Granite; Position Quality Flag). Personnel Tracking Console; North/South Access Scanners; Warehouse System (Mosslight; Backorder Exception Slip);

Document units:
S269: The Duty Planner revises priorities when asset condition, access forecasts, or resource availability changes, and communicates the resulting plan to affected teams.
S270: Weather Service provides forecast conditions and confidence information for planned work areas and vessel routes.
S271: Metocean Buoy observations give the team a local reference for checking forecast trends and current sea state.
S272: Weather Analyst compares forecast data with recent observations before advising on the reliability of a work window.
S273: Forecast confidence is considered alongside the predicted conditions rather than treated as a substitute for operational limits.
S274: The Duty Planner checks that the expected conditions remain within the limits for the task, transfer method, and vessel.
S275: Low confidence near a limit leads to more conservative planning and a shorter review interval.
S276: A Weather Hold is applied when conditions are outside the approved limits or the available evidence is insufficient to support safe work.
S277: The Marine Coordinator reviews access options and vessel availability when a work window narrows.
S278: The Vessel Master receives the Transfer Manifest Addendum before departure.
S279: The Crew Transfer Vessel proceeds only when the Vessel Master considers the approach and transfer conditions acceptable.
S280: A forecast that improves does not by itself release a hold, because the team also checks current observations and the task-specific limits.
S281: The Service Operations Vessel may provide a more stable work platform, but its operating limits still govern whether work can proceed.
S282: Vessel Standby is used when transit or station keeping remains possible but personnel transfer or task execution is not justified.
S283: The Marine Coordinator reassesses the route when wind direction, wave conditions, or visibility changes materially.
S284: The Vessel Master can pause or abort an approach when observed conditions differ from the forecast or deteriorate during transit.
S285: Maintenance Planning Engine produces the Deferred Task Rationale when weather prevents a planned task from proceeding.
S286: The rationale supports later reprioritization without implying that the task is safe under the current conditions.
S287: Quiet Harbor blocks a route change when the required authorization is incomplete.
S288: Blue Granite provides vessel position information for review against the planned route and operating area.
S289: The team considers forecast uncertainty when deciding whether to commit crews, fuel, and vessel time to a remote work site.
S290: When conditions are changing rapidly, the Marine Coordinator seeks an updated forecast before confirming a departure or transfer plan.
